text:
Kailer Yamamoto is back from injured reserve and picked up right where he left off. Utah placed him on IR on Nov. 8, he returned on Nov. 11, and his minutes went up, not down: over 18 a night in his first four games back, including three assists against San Jose. He has 11 points in 13 games.

The underlying numbers are startling for a player who has bounced from Edmonton to Seattle to Utah. The Mammoth get 65% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, ten points better than without him, and he's getting to dangerous chances at nearly double last season's rate. He's shooting just 10.7%, so the goals (three) are trailing the chances.

His scoring rate of 3.2 points per 60 sits above our talent range of 1.8 to 2.8, so expect some cooling there. But Evolving-Hockey had him 53rd among 401 forwards last season, in the 98th percentile for taking chances away, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking pegged him as a setup man who does his damage off the rush. Utah hasn't won since he came back. He isn't the reason.
